prompt:
Describe the real object seen in these images. Return JSON with
max_length_m and parts. Use one to five material-bearing components. Each part has
name, evidence, material_id, construction_id, v, a and parameter.
Choose material_id by number from this list: 1: foam, 2: rubber, 3: plastic, 4: wood, 5: aluminum, 6: steel, 7: glass, 8: ceramic, 9: silicone, 10: paper_cardboard, 11: fabric, 12: leather, 13: stone.
Use construction_id 1 for filled material, 2 for a hollow thin shell and 3 for an
unfilled lattice or assembly. For each component, give a positive relative size
weight v (1–100) and a visible surface weight a (0–100), with at least one positive
a. The weights need not sum to 100. Never list a void as a part. Set parameter to
1 for filled material, wall thickness in millimeters for a shell, or the material
fill fraction strictly between 0 and 1 for an unfilled assembly. Give a positive
max_length_m. Return JSON only. Do not estimate mass.
local_dimension_prompt:
Describe the material-bearing components of this panel-built
object in the images. Its estimated longest dimension is {length} m. Exclude the
empty space inside or between panels. Return JSON with groups, each containing
name, material, kind, count and dimensions. Materials: {materials}.
Use sheet for panels (area_m2 per piece, thickness_mm; add solid_fraction between
0 and 1 for grilles or perforated panels). Use box (three dimensions_mm) only for
compact solid components. For a support use tube (length_m, diameter_mm,
wall_mm) or rod (length_m, diameter_mm). Include visible components and mark any
plausible hidden component in its name. Counts are positive integers. Do not
estimate mass.
